findings.name: xunliuDesign (Xun Liu) GitHub account
findings.what_it_does: Xun Liu's account: 15 public repos (13 own, 2 MIT Notion forks), 12 followers, 20 stars. Own work: mapping, AI4GH, false-creek-2100. It hosts none of hairline, anatomy or text-to-cad (all 404 there); it only starred them.
findings.how_we_use_it: Read its stars list as Xun's curated tool shelf: the three tools lead it, then Rhino/Grasshopper MCPs, Claude skills and agent tutorials. Mine it for ideas; treat stars as pointers, not endorsements or licences.
findings.last_activity: Newest push 2026-07-17 (des212-2026, a redirect-only stub pointing to GenEnv); newest substantive own repo false-creek-2100, 2026-06-11
findings.license: n/a (per repo; none of the 13 own repos has one; the 2 forks are MIT)
findings.risks: Handle is xunliuDesign, not 'XunLiu Design'. GitHub org xlstudio belongs to someone else. Starring is not an endorsement. Pronoun and intent behind the stars unknown.
findings.saves: Avoids searching wrong accounts.

findings.name: GenEnv (GenEnv Lab) organisation
findings.what_it_does: Lab/course org, 9 public repos: rhino-gh-mcp, genenv-site, des212-2026, Thermal-Sandbox-Web (a fork), ai4dm-site, ai-agents-for-architects, sala-tech-knowledge-tree, Arch540_2026, arch540-a1-toolkit. No public members. agents_demo is a folder inside Arch540_2026, not a repo.
findings.how_we_use_it: Primary instructor-owned source for course patterns (agent demos, Rhino MCP, validators, sun data). Check weekly until 10 Dec for new student tools; log each reuse with licence status and who gave permission.
findings.license: Only rhino-gh-mcp has a LICENSE (MIT). The other 8 have none (verified from full file trees and API licence=null).
findings.maintainer: GenEnv / UBC SALA (Xun Liu per course context)
findings.risks: No licence on 8 of 9 repos means all rights reserved, so code reuse needs written permission. Authorship per repo unconfirmed; one repo is a fork of a non-GenEnv user's work.
findings.saves: One org to check for course-approved building blocks.

findings.name: hairline (lucasmarkes/hairline)
findings.what_it_does: MIT library of 33 pointer-reactive isometric line-drawn SVG figures for React or any DOM; no runtime dependencies, one shared animation loop. Ships agent skills hairline-create (draws a new figure as one HTML file) and hairline-adopt (rebuilds an SVG).
findings.how_we_use_it: v1: vendor 3-5 figures (empty canvas, onboarding, module cards) at pinned v0.5.1, not latest. Adopt its ten rules as our linework and motion spec. Run hairline-create at most once for a tower figure.
findings.last_activity: 2026-10-14 (v0.5.1; six releases from v0.1.0-rc.0 on 1 Oct)
findings.license: MIT (c) Lucas Marques; GitHub API confirms MIT; monorepo package.json has no license field
findings.popularity: 2.55k stars, 157 forks, 5 open issues+PRs (21 Oct 2026); HN post 4 Oct: 2 points, 0 comments; 1 X post; 1 third-party article; 21st.dev listing
findings.risks: Single maintainer, repo created 1 Oct, so breaking changes likely. GitHub description still says 'Six' figures (README says 33). Figures are generic, not architectural. Monorepo dev needs Node 22+ and pnpm.
findings.saves: Hours of hand-coded SVG animation.

findings.name: anatomy (wheresryan22/anatomy)
findings.what_it_does: MIT agent skill that builds an interactive isometric SVG figure (optional WebGL shaders, beta 3D) explaining an idea as a real machine. Ships a drawing kit, geometry audit, headless-Chrome checks and A4/Letter print sheets. Slow by design.
findings.how_we_use_it: Roadmap: one or two hero explainers (sun path, stack-effect shaft) for the landing page or boards, Figure tier only, with a time and token cap; never ask for 'the tower'. Reuse its geometry-audit and zero-loose-line checks as our drawing QA.
findings.popularity: 17.8k stars, 1.4k forks, 61 open issues+PRs; created 8 Oct 2026; HN: 2 posts, 2 points, 0 comments; 4+ independent X, YouTube and Medium posts, enthusiastic but mostly descriptive
findings.risks: SKILL.md rates a whole building Epic (6 h+, do not start without asking). Reported 30 min to about 2 h per figure. Kit needs Node 20.10+, the installer CLI Node 22.20+, plus Chrome. Examples are machines; sheets are A4, not A2.
findings.saves: Design time only; Figure/Hero/Epic tiers help cap spend.

findings.name: text-to-cad (earthtojake/text-to-cad)
findings.what_it_does: MIT Claude Code plugin and skills letting agents generate STEP, GLB, STL, 3MF and DXF from text or images via build123d and Open CASCADE (cadgen), with viewer, drawings, DFM and printing skills. Mechanical focus: parts, robots, G-code.
findings.how_we_use_it: Roadmap: optional local experiment for odd-shaped massing or facade parts, GLB into our viewer. Not the v1 massing node: tower massing is extruded floor plates and it cannot write .3dm or IFC. Never bundle it in the browser app.
findings.popularity: 22.1k stars, 2.2k forks, 29 open issues+PRs; open-sourced 22 Apr 2026; HN thread 1 May: 186 points, 48 comments, mixed (about 5 of 17 commenters report supervised use, about 6 doubt spatial reasoning or the benchmarks)
findings.risks: Needs uv (not installed). Smart App Control blocks OCP unless off or under WSL; turning it off is irreversible, so never ask anyone to. Telemetry and daily update check default on: set CADGEN_TELEMETRY=0 and CADGEN_UPDATE_CHECK=0.
findings.saves: Would avoid building a CAD kernel and viewer, but only for mechanical parts.

findings.name: anatomy-community gallery
findings.what_it_does: Gallery where figures are submitted as source (build.mjs, figure.json) by agent script or Gist plus issue bot. CI rebuilds in a locked sandbox with a two-run determinism check, publishes previews on a branch; maintainer reviews.
findings.how_we_use_it: Model for our module hub: source-only submissions, sandboxed rebuild, preview, per-module licence field, takedown by deleting a folder. Read its CONTRIBUTING and workflow files before copying any. Design now, implement in v1.
findings.license: Root LICENSE is MIT (c) Ryan and contributors, with CC-BY-4.0 for figures that say so in figure.json; GitHub API shows NOASSERTION because of that extra line
findings.risks: Open-PR backlog hints at review load. Sandbox hardening not audited by us. CI minutes and Node build dependency. Per-figure licences vary.
findings.saves: A proven moderation workflow instead of inventing one.

findings.name: Thermal-Sandbox-Web (GenEnv fork of christinachiu)
findings.what_it_does: Static app comparing annual solar load on a 215 x 130 m Winnipeg site (University of Manitoba), baseline vs scenario. Two JSON files drive it: Rhino-derived geometry and about 20k Ladybug/Radiance irradiance points. Three.js 0.160 viewer inside one 5 MB HTML file.
findings.how_we_use_it: Core reference for sun and energy nodes: precompute irradiance in Python, emit typed JSON, render in browser. Copy its meta-block idea (units, sources, notes, open-sky total, derived formulas) into our output schema; compare baseline and scenario point by point. Re-implement; copy no code.
findings.license: None (5-path tree has no LICENSE; API null; upstream also none)
findings.popularity: Fork: 1 star, 1 open PR; upstream: 0 stars, 1 fork
findings.risks: No licence; author's affiliation unknown and permission must come from the upstream owner. Fork is 3 weeks behind upstream. Winnipeg data, not Vancouver. Ladybug, the generating tool, is AGPL-3.0.
findings.saves: Output-schema and unit conventions (kWh/m2/yr; solar reduction = 1 - load / open-sky total) for sun and energy modules.

findings.name: des212-2026 (GenEnv)
findings.what_it_does: UBC DES 212 Design Media II archive: Grasshopper tutorial pages with video, lecture slides, assignment briefs and a syllabus PDF. README says tutorials include downloadable .gh and .3dm files (Module 1-3 folders; individual files not opened). Built from a Canvas export.
findings.how_we_use_it: Roadmap: onboarding path for teammates new to Grasshopper; link to it, do not copy. Use its module-by-module tutorial structure as a model for documenting our module cards.
findings.risks: No licence; course material owned by the instructor. Build script is kept offline, so the site cannot be regenerated from the repo. The xunliuDesign copy is only a redirect stub.
findings.saves: Teammate onboarding time on Grasshopper.

findings.name: rhino-gh-mcp (GenEnv)
findings.what_it_does: MIT MCP server plus Rhino 8 and Grasshopper C# plugins (v0.2.6): an LLM reads and edits a live canvas, captures the viewport, runs commands. A Scenario dropdown (Inspect, Tune, Coach, Execute, Author) gates AI access. Bundles four skills.
findings.how_we_use_it: v1, optional bridge for teammates who model in Rhino: Claude tunes sliders and reads definitions. Not our web import path (use rhino3dm.js). Copy Scenario gating as per-node AI permission levels; reuse bundled skills as module recipes.
findings.risks: Rhino 8 licence and Windows desktop only; early version; Ladybug must be installed. McNeel forum threads report setup failures and silent script errors with Rhino MCP servers generally, not tied to this repo.
findings.saves: Skips writing a RhinoCommon plugin and MCP server.

findings.name: Arch540_2026 course repo (agents_demo)
findings.what_it_does: Four runnable Claude Code demos: A writing, B test-fit, C design-space, D team (about 10 agents). Contains CLAUDE.md, check.py, evaluate.py, Pareto front.py, limits.json, hooks and a family-explorer subagent. Needs numpy, scipy, shapely, matplotlib.
findings.how_we_use_it: Core: copy the patterns for our evaluation modules, not the code: deterministic evaluator as the only source of numbers, JSON in/out, Pareto front, hook refusing failing output, UNRESOLVED after six revisions. Ask Xun for a licence now.
findings.license: None (verified: 394-path tree has no LICENSE; API null)
findings.risks: No licence. Demo rules (3 m setback, 40 m height) are teaching values, not Vancouver bylaws. D_team can exhaust a Pro 5-hour allowance. Only prompts and file lists read, not all code.
findings.saves: Large token saving: numbers come from scripts, not the LLM.

findings.name: arch540-a1-toolkit (15 student Vancouver-regulation tools)
findings.what_it_does: Static index of 15 student tools on Vancouver rules (Curbside, Stair Core, R3 Feasibility, Solar Shading Explorer, MassShadeLight, Lotwise, Downtown Massing, Massing Studio, Vista...). Each is a JSON card with tool and repo links.
findings.how_we_use_it: Core: mine as a reading list for policy, sun, view and code modules and as collaborators to ask. Cards give tool_url and repo_url. Read the 11 unread cards before choosing what to port.
findings.risks: No licence on index or most tools. Many are one-person prototypes with unverified rules. Authors are classmates, so credit and consent matter.
findings.saves: Weeks of rule research if rules are re-verified from bylaws.

findings.name: Downtown Massing Tool (xubynii/dtmass)
findings.what_it_does: Static WebGL tool by Sinnie Choi testing downtown Vancouver tower massings against VBBL 2025, Downtown ODP 4912, floor-plate bulletin, downtown guidelines, solar access guidelines (Sep 2025), views and parking; reads .3dm. README says inputs need manual verification.
findings.how_we_use_it: Core, as a reading list: use its rule-to-document mapping to seed the policy module's source list; re-derive numeric rules from the cited documents as editable team assumptions. Copy code or tables only with written permission.
findings.license: None (verified: 59-path tree has no LICENSE; API null)
findings.risks: All rights reserved by default. Author flags ODP density, height and view-cone inputs as manually verified. Student prototype; rule accuracy not checked by us.
findings.saves: Rule discovery: a mapped list of governing documents for the block.

findings.name: Vista (RuijieLiu6/vancouver-tall-view-tool)
findings.what_it_does: Browser tool testing a massing footprint against City of Vancouver mapped view corridors (open-data plan polygons only), rendering approximate views from estimated origins and exporting a PDF; imports .3dm and .obj locally (vendors rhino3dm.js). Public repo is a built bundle of a private project.
findings.how_we_use_it: Core, internal asset: first port for the view-corridor node. Reuse the open-data pipeline (view-cones, SRTM terrain, OSM buildings), .3dm import and PDF report; add cone height limits from the Public Views Guidelines. Add a LICENSE once ownership is confirmed.
findings.license: None today (only vendored rhino3dm MIT). Data: Open Government Licence (Vancouver, BC), OSM ODbL, SRTM, Inter font OFL
findings.maintainer: Ruijie Liu (RuijieLiu6); handle matches the requesting user's account (to confirm)
findings.risks: Context model is derived from a supplied studio Rhino model; check permission before licensing it. ODbL and OGL data keep their own terms. Footprint overlap only, no heights; README disclaims compliance. Source is private.
findings.saves: A working view-cone data pipeline and import path, with no consent wait.

findings.name: Massing Studio (clcabana/massing-studio)
findings.what_it_does: Python/FastAPI pydantic rule engine with a JS port: live VBBL 2025 Part 3 and Zoning By-law 3575 checks with clause citations (occupancy, fire separation, exits, washrooms, FSR, height); exports Excel and Rhino .3dm. Labelled a draft for professional review.
findings.how_we_use_it: Core, as a reading list for the MEP/code module: study its clause-cited rule structure and the 'draft for professional review' label; Python engine fits our stack. Copy code or tables only with written licence from the author.
findings.license: None (verified: 82-path tree has no LICENSE; API null)
findings.risks: All rights reserved by default. Which by-law governs our block must be verified (Downtown ODP vs 3575). Dual Python/JS engines can drift. Early.
findings.saves: Weeks of code-rule transcription, if licensed; built-in citations.

findings.name: AI4GH (xunliuDesign)
findings.what_it_does: C# Grasshopper components bringing GenAI into Grasshopper via API (folders Robot_GH and 'Nano Banana_GH'). README is one line; models used and install not documented.
findings.how_we_use_it: Roadmap: reference for how Xun wires image-generation APIs into Grasshopper nodes; mirror its typed inputs and outputs in our AI-render node. Request the README and a licence.
findings.risks: Almost no documentation; Grasshopper/Rhino only; no licence; 11 months old.
findings.saves: Design reference for an AI-render node.

findings.name: false-creek-2100 (xunliuDesign)
findings.what_it_does: No-build static JS prototype: pixel sea-level-rise sandbox for South False Creek. Paint seawalls, marshes, canals; bathtub-plus-connectivity flood model; keyboard shortcuts; PNG export stamped with scenario and metrics. Python script builds OSM and Terrarium grid.
findings.how_we_use_it: Roadmap: pattern for a light, engaging interaction loop and metric-stamped exports in presentation mode; its 10 m grid data script could seed a flood/resilience module near False Creek.
findings.license: Code: none (verified: 19-path tree has no LICENSE); data ODbL and Terrarium
findings.risks: v0.1 single commit. README says it is not a flood map or engineering advice. Near-shore terrain synthesised.
findings.saves: Small, readable example of interaction design and export stamping.

findings.name: sala-tech-knowledge-tree
findings.what_it_does: Faculty-verified map of Grasshopper tutorials: one-file site, content-gh.json as source of truth with prerequisites and status, validate.py checking IDs and prerequisite cycles on each pull request, spreadsheet templates for bulk contributions, CLAUDE.md.
findings.how_we_use_it: v1: model our module manifest and CI validation on it (IDs, dependency cycles, source fields). Reuse the spreadsheet-to-JSON bulk contribution idea as a pattern. Also a Grasshopper learning path for onboarding.
findings.risks: No licence, so copy the design, not the code. Baked-in JSON blob needs regeneration to edit; public contribution page not yet enabled.
findings.saves: Ready validation design for module graphs.

findings.name: ai4dm-site (GenEnv)
findings.what_it_does: Student-facing collections on generative AI in landscape representation (v1, v2). The v3 platform (atlas, gallery, prompt lab, studio taking your own API key) is in progress; its source is a separate private repo. build.py --public strips restricted images.
findings.how_we_use_it: Roadmap: ask Xun to show v3 UX as reference for our AI render step and bring-your-own-key flow; adopt the public-build filter that excludes copyrighted reference images.
findings.risks: Platform code is private and unlicensed; static Notion exports; only the README was read.
findings.saves: UX reference; avoids rework on BYO-key handling.

findings.name: ai-agents-for-architects (GenEnv)
findings.what_it_does: Chinese-language DigitalFUTURES 2026 agent workshop kit: demos 00_anatomy to 09_design_tools, switchable between Claude and DeepSeek via config, cheatsheets and glossary, run_pipeline.py. Not the anatomy skill despite the folder name.
findings.how_we_use_it: Roadmap: copy the one-config provider switch idea for our Claude/OpenAI/other model layer; use its cheatsheet format for onboarding docs.
findings.risks: Chinese-language; no licence; teaching demos, not production code.
findings.saves: Provider-switch pattern for multi-model calls.

findings.name: skills-for-architects (AlpacaLabsLLC)
findings.what_it_does: MIT Claude Code/Codex plugin with 61 architecture skills (zoning-envelope with interactive 3D buildable envelope, occupancy-calculator, environmental-analysis, mobility-analysis, spec and EPD tools) plus 8 agents, 8 rules, 4 hooks. NYC-centric. Starred by Xun.
findings.how_we_use_it: v1: borrow skill structure, code-citation rules and 'marked for professional review' outputs; adapt zoning-envelope and occupancy-calculator ideas to Vancouver. Install only 4-5 skills to avoid context bloat.
findings.risks: NYC data and rules; 61 skills can bloat context and tokens; many FF&E skills irrelevant; third-party maintenance.
findings.saves: Weeks of prompt design; token saving only if few skills are loaded.

findings.name: rhinomcp (jingcheng-chen)
findings.what_it_does: MIT Python MCP server (uvx rhinomcp@latest) plus RhinoCommon plugin: create and edit Rhino geometry, inspect/place/wire/solve Grasshopper, run RhinoScript or C#, capture viewports. Rhino 8 on Windows and Mac; TCP on 127.0.0.1:1999.
findings.how_we_use_it: Roadmap: alternative or complement to rhino-gh-mcp for Rhino users; uvx suits our Python-first Windows setup. Optional developer convenience, not the web import path.
findings.risks: README states the TCP link is unauthenticated and execution tools are broad; keep loopback only. Rhino 8 licence needed. Needs uv (not installed).
findings.saves: A broader tool set than rhino-gh-mcp without writing a bridge.

findings.name: RhinoAI (mcneel)
findings.what_it_does: MIT official McNeel repo: MCP server and Rhino plugin connecting Claude Desktop/Code, Copilot, Codex, Gemini CLI and local models to Rhino; connector v0.1.6; docs site; discussion on the Rhino Discourse forum.
findings.how_we_use_it: Roadmap: track as the likely long-term supported Rhino-AI bridge; evaluate before locking in a community MCP. Confirm which Rhino version it supports before recommending it to teammates.
findings.risks: Early (v0.1.6). Default branch is rhino-9.x, with rhino-9.0 and rhino-10.x branches; README and getting-started page do not state a supported Rhino version, so it may need Rhino 9 WIP.
findings.saves: Avoids maintaining our own Rhino bridge if it stabilises.

findings.name: openai/codex-plugin-cc
findings.what_it_does: Apache-2.0 plugin letting Claude Code call OpenAI Codex: /codex:review, /codex:adversarial-review, /codex:rescue, background jobs. Needs a ChatGPT account or OpenAI API key and Node 18.18+. Starred by Xun.
findings.how_we_use_it: v1 dev workflow: cheap second-opinion adversarial review of module logic and code using OpenAI, matching the wish to use both vendors. Pin a version and keep the optional Stop-hook review gate off.
findings.risks: Slower cadence and large issue backlog; spends OpenAI quota; review gate can loop usage; sends project code to a second vendor; Node needed (not installed).
findings.saves: Catches logic errors early, reducing rework tokens; adds cost per review.

findings.name: Physalia (aarcThom)
findings.what_it_does: Rhino 8 (Windows) plugin to build Grasshopper definitions by prompting LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, Claude Code SDK), with MCP, PDF context, presets and error-fixing loops. Install section says TODO.
findings.how_we_use_it: Read-only for ideas on staged builds and runtime-error repair loops. Do not copy code: AGPL-3.0 would force AGPL terms on our release.
findings.risks: AGPL copyleft; install undocumented; Rhino-only; small community.
findings.saves: Nothing directly; avoids licence contamination if rejected.

findings.name: rhino-grasshopper-mcp (dongwoosuk)
findings.what_it_does: Beta (v0.1.0) MCP server for Rhino/Grasshopper with remote Python execution, .gh parsing, templates and scikit-learn 'ML auto-layout' (clustering, K-NN positions). Only 3 commits.
findings.how_we_use_it: Do not adopt. Better-maintained options exist (rhino-gh-mcp, rhinomcp, RhinoAI). Its auto-layout idea could inspire canvas tidy-up later.
findings.risks: Very early; 'not found in any other tool' claim is unsupported; localhost:8080 listener; little maintenance evidence.
findings.saves: Avoids a dead-end dependency.

findings.name: rhino3dm (mcneel)
findings.what_it_does: MIT OpenNURBS-based toolkit in Python, JavaScript/WASM and .NET that reads and writes .3dm files without Rhino. PyPI 8.35.0 ships a cp313 Windows wheel; the npm package rhino3dm.js runs in browsers and Node.
findings.how_we_use_it: Core: browser .3dm import through rhino3dm.js (Vista already vendors it) and Python .3dm export of generated massing. Fits our Python 3.13 setup. Final choice belongs to the import packet.
findings.risks: WASM size and load time not measured by us. Only what OpenNURBS exposes: no Grasshopper or Rhino plug-in data.
findings.saves: Avoids writing a .3dm parser and writer; no Rhino licence needed.

findings.name: web-ifc (ThatOpen/engine_web-ifc)
findings.what_it_does: JavaScript/WASM library to read and write IFC files at native speed in browser or Node; part of That Open Company's open BIM stack (engine_components, MIT, adds viewer and BIM tools).
findings.how_we_use_it: v1: IFC import for massing and program tagging in the browser; consider That Open components if we need an IFC viewer. Hand deeper evaluation (large tower files, API stability) to the import packet.
findings.risks: MPL-2.0 file-level copyleft; not tested by us on large IFC files; That Open API churn unknown.
findings.saves: Avoids writing an IFC parser.

findings.name: xyflow (React Flow / Svelte Flow)
findings.what_it_does: MIT node-based UI libraries: React Flow 12 (@xyflow/react) and Svelte Flow, with custom nodes, handles, minimap, controls and a shared @xyflow/system helper package.
findings.how_we_use_it: Core candidate for the Grasshopper-like canvas: one custom node per module, typed ports, run-all or step-in. Final framework choice belongs to the canvas packet; read its commercial-use terms before shipping.
findings.risks: Maintainers ask commercial users for sponsorship; ties us to React or Svelte; performance with large graphs untested by us. Only the README was read.
findings.saves: Weeks of canvas pan, zoom, drag and wiring code.

principles.principle: Hairline rule 'hit': pointer tests run against the resting pose, so hover never flickers.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Canvas nodes, ports and wires use static hit areas, not animated geometry, so hover and drag stay stable.

principles.principle: Hairline rules 'accent' and 'quiet': the stroke is the only highlight; no fills, glows or words inside the figure.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Keep a small calm palette and reserve one signal colour for FALSE ASSUMPTION so it never loses meaning; no decorative glow or badge noise.

principles.principle: Hairline rule 'rest': the resting state is composed with one bright mark showing where to look.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Every screen has one focal point and one next action (for example 'run module'), which keeps users focused without nudging tricks.

principles.principle: Hairline rules 'cost' and 'clock': animate only when needed, pause offscreen, long ease-out for discrete choices, springs for continuous tracking; reduced-motion lands instantly.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Set a motion budget: one shared animation loop, pause when hidden, honour prefers-reduced-motion, skip redraws when values are unchanged (matters for large canvases).

principles.principle: Anatomy: 'the object is the explanation'; displayed numbers come from a running model and must be true.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Every number on screen comes from a module's computed output and cites its source or is flagged a team assumption; no placeholder or invented figures.

principles.principle: Anatomy verifies visuals mechanically: geometry audit, zero loose line ends, headless screenshots at desktop and 390 px, close-ups.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Add automated visual QA (Playwright screenshots at desktop and phone width, overlap/clearance audit) before a module or board ships; cheaper in tokens than visual re-prompting.

principles.principle: Anatomy sizes work in tiers (Figure under about an hour, Hero 2-4 h, Epic 6 h+ and never started unasked; a whole building counts as Epic) with a working page inside the first hour.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Give AI-built visuals a size tier and time/token budget; ask before building anything larger than the default tier, and never request a whole-tower figure.

principles.principle: Arch540 C_design_space: a provided evaluator is the only trusted source of numbers and is never edited by the agent.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Each evaluation module is deterministic code with typed JSON outputs; the LLM orchestrates and explains but never invents metrics. Saves tokens and prevents hallucinated numbers.

principles.principle: Arch540 B_testfit: a hook refuses failing output, at most six revisions, then stop and end with UNRESOLVED; never claim success without a passing check.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Add an UNRESOLVED state and an iteration cap to every AI-assisted module run, and gate outputs on a passing check rather than the model's claim.

principles.principle: rhino-gh-mcp gates AI access with scenario modes: Inspect, Tune, Coach (default), Execute, Author.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Give each node and the whole canvas an AI permission level, defaulting to read/suggest, so users stay in control and edits are traceable.

principles.principle: text-to-cad layering: skills are the product, shared core has no UI imports, apps never import apps, heavy kernel stays out of the server process, one pinned command per skill.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Structure our repo as core (graph and module contracts), ui, and apps, with heavy geometry/solar code in separate workers and pinned, reproducible commands for every module.

principles.principle: anatomy-community submits source, not built output; CI rebuilds in a locked sandbox with a two-run determinism check, previews, human review, per-item licence.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Community modules are uploaded as source plus manifest, rebuilt deterministically in a sandbox, previewed, reviewed, and carry a licence and source-citation field.

principles.principle: sala-tech-knowledge-tree keeps content as JSON with a validator for IDs and prerequisite cycles on every pull request, plus a verified-status field.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Module manifests are schema-validated in CI (unique IDs, no dependency cycles, required sources); status fields show verified, team assumption or FALSE ASSUMPTION.

principles.principle: Massing Studio and skills-for-architects mark code and zoning output as a draft for professional review and cite clauses.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Every compliance result shows clause citation, edition date and a 'draft, not a compliance determination' label.

principles.principle: Thermal-Sandbox-Web ships its data with a meta block (units, sources, notes, open-sky total, derived formulas) and compares baseline with scenario point by point.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Every module output carries a meta block (units, source citations, data version, derived formula, team-assumption flag) and supports baseline-vs-scenario comparison on identical points.

recommendations.decision: Treat hairline, anatomy and text-to-cad as third-party MIT repos that Xun starred, not as Xun's own tools. Email Xun once to ask why they were shared, plus for: licence statements on the GenEnv course repos, the ai4dm v3 demo, D_team run notes and the AI4GH README.
recommendations.rationale: All three return 404 on xunliuDesign and lead its stars list; owners are lucasmarkes, wheresryan22, earthtojake. MIT lets us reuse with attribution, so the email is not blocking. No mention of them in six GenEnv READMEs checked.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Assuming Xun authored them (false); waiting on a reply before using them (they are MIT).

recommendations.decision: Licence plan with a dated fallback. Today (21 Oct) the team emails Xun, Sinnie Choi (dtmass), Claudio Cabana (Massing Studio) and christinachiu (Thermal-Sandbox-Web) asking for MIT or written permission. If no reply by 1 Nov, use those repos only as reading lists: write our own code and re-derive rules from the cited bylaws. Log every reuse with licence and permission.
recommendations.rationale: Verified from full file trees: no LICENSE and API licence null on Arch540_2026, arch540-a1-toolkit, dtmass, massing-studio, Vista, AI4GH and every GenEnv repo except rhino-gh-mcp. Default is all rights reserved; core is due 13 Nov.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Copying code or rule tables without permission; waiting past 1 Nov; re-transcribing all bylaws before asking.

recommendations.decision: Core (by 13 Nov): adopt the Arch540 agents_demo pattern as our module contract: deterministic Python evaluator (numpy, scipy, shapely), JSON in/out, Pareto front, hook refusing failing output, UNRESOLVED stop after six revisions. Copy the pattern, not the files, until a licence arrives.
recommendations.rationale: Moves numbers out of the LLM into scripts, which saves tokens and keeps results reproducible; matches the course method. numpy, scipy and shapely have cp313 Windows wheels on PyPI.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: LLM-computed metrics (hallucination and token cost); copying demo thresholds as Vancouver values (teaching values).

recommendations.decision: Core: build the sun and energy nodes on the Thermal-Sandbox-Web pattern: precompute irradiance in Python, emit typed JSON with a meta block, render in browser. Decide the Ladybug question first: Ladybug and Honeybee are AGPL-3.0, so run them only as an optional user-side precompute, or evaluate pvlib (BSD-3) as an in-platform alternative.
recommendations.rationale: The repo shows a working Rhino to Ladybug/Radiance to JSON to browser chain with explicit units and provenance. Ladybug LICENSE headers read AGPL-3.0, which would constrain our own licence if linked in-process.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Copying its code (no licence); importing Ladybug in-process without a licence decision; building a solar engine from scratch.

recommendations.decision: Browser path first: use rhino3dm.js (MIT) for .3dm, web-ifc (MPL-2.0) for IFC and an MIT node-canvas library (xyflow candidate), with three.js for viewing, and hand final choices to the import and canvas packets. Rhino MCPs (rhino-gh-mcp, rhinomcp, RhinoAI) stay an optional bridge for teammates who model in Rhino.
recommendations.rationale: The product is browser-based; the Rhino MCPs need a licensed Rhino 8 session and do not feed the web import path. Licences and wheels checked this round; no browser tests run.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Making a Rhino MCP the import path; Physalia (AGPL-3.0); dongwoosuk's repo (3 commits).

recommendations.decision: v1 AI massing node: Claude writes a small Python generator (shapely floor plates, trimesh GLB for the viewer, rhino3dm .3dm export) under the Arch540 evaluator contract. Move text-to-cad to roadmap as an optional local experiment.
recommendations.rationale: Tower massing is mostly extruded plates, needing no B-rep kernel. text-to-cad targets mechanical parts, cannot write .3dm or IFC, and adds uv, OCP and a Smart App Control risk. trimesh is pure Python.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: text-to-cad as v1 dependency; bundling it in the web client; hand-writing a CAD kernel.

recommendations.decision: Visual assets: v1, use hairline for 3-5 figures (empty canvas, onboarding, module cards) pinned to v0.5.1 and vendored, with its ten rules as our linework and motion spec. Roadmap, anatomy for one or two Figure-tier explainers (sun path, stack-effect shaft) with a time and token cap, never a whole tower.
recommendations.rationale: Hairline is MIT, dependency-free and reduced-motion aware, but one maintainer and six releases in 14 days make pinning essential. anatomy rates a building as Epic (6 h+) and its sheets are A4.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Tracking hairline latest; generating all board diagrams with anatomy; hand-coded pointer-reactive SVG.

recommendations.decision: v1: copy the anatomy-community submission pipeline and the sala-tech-knowledge-tree validator for our module hub (source-only upload, sandbox rebuild, preview, schema and cycle checks, per-module licence and source fields). Read the repo's CONTRIBUTING and workflow files before reusing any.
recommendations.rationale: Two working, open examples of moderated community contribution. anatomy-community root LICENSE is MIT with per-figure CC-BY-4.0 (verified); sala has no licence, so copy its design only.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Open uploads of built artifacts; unreviewed forks; building a custom marketplace before the first 10 modules exist.

recommendations.decision: Environment before any pilot: install Node 22+ LTS and uv once (for example via winget; confirm package IDs) and record versions in the project README. Each teammate checks Smart App Control (WSL if on; never ask anyone to turn it off) and sets CADGEN_TELEMETRY=0 and CADGEN_UPDATE_CHECK=0.
recommendations.rationale: Read-only check on the session machine (21 Oct): Smart App Control off, WSL not installed, uv and Node not installed, and the default python on PATH is 3.9.13 while 3.13 exists via the py launcher. Other machines unknown.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Disabling Smart App Control (irreversible without reinstalling Windows); relying on system Python.

recommendations.decision: v1: add openai/codex-plugin-cc (Apache-2.0) to the dev workflow for adversarial review with OpenAI, pinned to a known version, review gate off; keep product-side OpenAI calls (GPT, gpt-image) as a separate API integration.
recommendations.rationale: Meets the wish to use both vendors and gives a second opinion on module logic. No push since 8 Jul and 536 open issues+PRs, so pin and expect little upstream movement.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Running both vendors on every edit (cost); using the plugin as product runtime (it is a dev tool).
